newsitem.title: UK: Refined peanut oil OK for allergic sufferers-study.
newsitem.headline: Refined peanut oil OK for allergic sufferers-study.

text.p: Refined peanut oil is probably safe for people who are badly allergic to peanuts, but unrefined oil might be dangerous, British researchers reported on Friday.
A study of 60 people with known peanut allergy -- which can kill -- showed that none reacted to the refined oil, the researchers reported in the British Medical Journal.
About 10 percent of allergic volunteers reacted to crude peanut oil, the team, led by Dr Jonathan Hourihane of Southampton General Hospital, said.
"Peanut allergy is the commonest cause of fatal and near-fatal allergic reactions to foods in the United States," they wrote.
It was becoming more recognised as a threat elsewhere, they added. Nonetheless it was vital for restaurant and catering staff to be more aware of food allergy.

"They must be aware of the risk to people with life-threatening reactions to foods of re-use of oils, especially after cooking foods that are known to be allergenic, such as peanuts, treenuts, fish and shellfish," they said.
They also said manufacturers should stop using the confusing term groundnut for peanut oil, and should clearly label refined and crude oils.
